stepTexts.heat_pan: Warm a cast-iron or heavy skillet over medium heat and melt the butter.
stepTexts.crisp_bacon: Lay in the bacon and cook until the edges are browned and crisp while the centre stays tender.
stepTexts.add_eggs: Move the bacon toward the sides of the pan, then crack the eggs into the open centre without breaking the yolks.
stepTexts.finish_eggs: Lower the heat and cook gently until the whites are set and the yolks are still soft.
stepTexts.season_serve: Finish with black pepper and serve immediately with toasted rustic bread.

miso_paste.name: Miso paste
miso_paste.note: soy sauce can be used for a lighter alternative

stepTexts.season_broth: Heat the broth gently and whisk in the miso until smooth. Keep it hot without letting it reduce aggressively.
stepTexts.cook_noodles: Cook the ramen noodles separately according to their package timing, then drain thoroughly.
stepTexts.fill_bowls: Divide the hot noodles between two bowls and ladle over enough broth to surround them.
stepTexts.add_toppings: Arrange the chashu, halved marinated eggs, narutomaki, spring onion, bean sprouts and nori over the noodles.
stepTexts.serve: Serve immediately while the broth and noodles are piping hot.

stepTexts.simmer_onion: Combine dashi, soy sauce, mirin and sugar in a small skillet. Add the onion and simmer until softened.
stepTexts.add_tonkatsu: Slice the fried pork cutlets into strips and lay them over the seasoned onion.
stepTexts.add_eggs: Beat the eggs only lightly, then pour them over the cutlets so distinct streaks of white and yolk remain.
stepTexts.steam_finish: Cover and cook briefly, stopping while the egg is still soft and creamy rather than fully firm.
stepTexts.assemble_bowl: Fill two bowls with hot rice, slide the pork-and-egg mixture on top and finish with peas or chives.

anko.name: Sweet red-bean paste (anko)
anko.note: hazelnut spread can be used as an alternative

stepTexts.whisk_base: Whisk the eggs with the sugar and honey until the mixture looks lighter and slightly foamy.
stepTexts.finish_batter: Mix the baking powder into the water, add it to the bowl and fold in the sifted flour until the batter is smooth.
stepTexts.rest_batter: Chill the batter for 15 minutes so it can settle before cooking.
stepTexts.cook_first_side: Heat a non-stick pan over low heat, wipe it with a very thin film of oil and spoon in small rounds of batter. Cook until bubbles appear on top.
stepTexts.cook_second_side: Turn each round and cook the second side briefly until evenly coloured.
stepTexts.fill_dorayaki: Let the cakes cool, then sandwich them in pairs with anko in the centre and gently press the edges into the classic rounded shape.

salt.name: Salt
salt.note: a small pinch plus a little for shaping

stepTexts.wash_cook_rice: Rinse the rice several times until the water runs much clearer. Cook it with the measured water, covered, over low heat.
stepTexts.rest_rice: Turn off the heat and leave the rice covered for 10 minutes before shaping.
stepTexts.make_filling: Mix the drained tuna with the Japanese mayonnaise and a small pinch of salt.
stepTexts.fill_shape: Moisten and lightly salt your hands. Flatten a portion of warm rice, add a little tuna filling in the centre, cover with more rice and shape into a compact triangle.
stepTexts.finish_nori: Wrap a strip of nori around the base. Add sesame or furikake if desired and serve while the rice is still pleasantly warm.
